data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 relocates the reliability gain from the checklist to 'social error-correction (inter-rater reliability)' but never addresses the problem's core requirement: identifying evidence within a single evaluation that distinguishes a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer. Because it attributes the gain to panel size/diversity and clerical-error detection, it implicitly treats any panel agreement as genuine correction — yet the problem demands a discriminator. A panel could exhibit high inter-rater reliability purely because all members applied the same checklist step identically (compliance), not because independent errors were caught. The argument provides no within-evaluation evidence that would separate these cases; the countercondition (groupthink) concerns a failure mode of the mechanism, not the required compliance-vs-gain discriminator.
